test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 17th November 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Pipes A and B can empty a full tank in 15 minutes and 20 minutes, respectively, while pipe C alone can fill the empty tank in 8 minutes. If pipes A, B and C are opened together, then in how many hours will the tank be filled?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of tank = LCM(15, 20, 8) = 120 units.

Efficiency of A = −120/15 = −8; B = −120/20 = −6; C = 120/8 = +15.

Combined efficiency = 15 − 8 − 6 = 1 unit/min.

Total time = 120 / 1 = 120 minutes.

Time in hours = 120 / 60 = 2 hours.

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Pipe A empties in 15 min, Pipe B empties in 20 min, Pipe C fills in 8 min.

Formula: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Pipes
 Time (min)
 Quantity (units)
 Efficiency
 
 

 A (Empty)
 15
 120
 −8
 
 

 B (Empty)
 20
 −6
 
 

 C (Fill)
 8
 15
 
 

⇒ Total Work (LCM of 15, 20, 8) = 120 units

⇒ Net efficiency of (A + B + C) = −8 − 6 + 15 = 1 unit/min

⇒ Total time taken to fill the tank = Total Work ÷ Net Efficiency

⇒ Time = 120 / 1 = 120 minutes

⇒ Time in hours = 120 / 60 = 2 hours

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Convention

Filling pipes (inlets) are assigned positive efficiency, while emptying pipes (outlets) are assigned negative efficiency.

Net Rate of Work

If multiple pipes work together, the net rate of work is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies.

Unit Conversion

To convert minutes to hours, divide the total minutes by 60 (1 hour = 60 minutes).</p
